content.comment_body: Is it possible to download data from the data logger without using the [product_name] programming software? I looked into a system called logomonitor, but that was for [article_no] and not [article_no]. I need a straightforward solution that doesn't involve accessing the device's data card directly. Any suggestions?
From what I know, the only way to read a data log from the device is by using the [product_name] software. Also, the device must be in stop mode.
I'm not sure I understood your answer. Are you saying that using the software is the only way to read the log file, and the machine must be stopped before downloading?

To access a data log file: 1.) Start the [product_name] software. 2.) Set the device to stop mode. 3.) Go to Tools > Transfer > Data Log upload. Using this process, only the last data log can be downloaded.

Hello, the sequence described is correct and managed through the software. Switching the device between STOP/RUN modes isn’t necessary directly on the device. Previously, I found a Windows tool that records PC activities—an executable file is generated and reproduces the recorded steps. If the machine can't be stopped, you could schedule execution of this file when downtime is possible, such as overnight. Regarding avoiding manual use of [product_name] software, with such recording tools you could automate operator actions: start the software, upload the data log, and save the file to a designated area, then revert system settings. Windows scheduled tasks can automate this daily when downtime allows. Each data log file will have a unique name, simplifying record management. Hope this helps.
A new question regarding data log retrieval has been moved to a separate thread. Best regards, [user_name] (Moderator)

analysis.insight_summary: Users need a straightforward way to download data logs from the [product_name] module without relying on dedicated software, aiming for an automated and secure approach. Present procedures available require the proprietary software and stopping the device, creating workflow limitations. Some alternatives using automation on Windows are discussed, but no direct, user-friendly solution exists for the newer module, indicating a need for better usability regarding data export.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy, automated, and secure method to extract data logs from the [product_name] module, without requiring specialized software or manual actions.
